package_info.package_manager: Custom/Manual Deployment (Go binary, not a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (multiple evolving versions, see SHA256 hashes)
package_info.why_malicious: BianLian is a ransomware and backdoor toolkit written in Go, deployed manually or via exploitation of vulnerabilities. It is designed to provide remote access, facilitate lateral movement, evade defenses, and ultimately encrypt victim data for ransom. The toolkit includes custom binaries, masquerades as legitimate system processes, manipulates system configuration, and exfiltrates or encrypts sensitive data.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Custom Go backdoor binary named svchost.exe, launched by a process other than services.exe.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the binary masquerades as svchost.exe and is launched by a non-standard parent process, enabling covert execution and persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: svchost.exe is a core Windows process and should only be launched by services.exe from its standard location. Launching it from a non-standard path or by a different parent process is a strong indicator of masquerading.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate svchost.exe should only be run from C:\Windows\System32 by services.exe. Here, a malicious binary is run from an arbitrary location by a non-standard parent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate software may use similar names for compatibility, but not for core system process names.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: netsh advfirewall firewall add rule name="Open RDP" dir=in action=allow protocol=TCP localport=3389
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code executes netsh to add a firewall rule that opens TCP port 3389, enabling Remote Desktop Protocol access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Opening RDP via netsh is a common tactic for enabling remote access, especially when performed by unauthorized or unknown processes.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Firewall rules should be managed by administrators, not by unknown or suspicious binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Administrators may open RDP for legitimate remote management.
key_indicators: Executed by unknown or suspicious process

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code issues a single ICMP ping to a target IP address to perform network reconnaissance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Single pings are often used for host discovery during lateral movement or reconnaissance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal user activity rarely involves scripted single pings to multiple hosts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network administrators may use ping for troubleshooting.
key_indicators: Frequent single pings to multiple hosts

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: wsmprovhost.exe (WinRM) launches PowerShell to drop a file on disk.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, wsmprovhost.exe mediates a remote PowerShell session that writes a file to disk, enabling remote payload delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: wsmprovhost.exe is typically used for legitimate remote management, but file drops via this process are a strong indicator of lateral movement or remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate WinRM sessions rarely drop arbitrary files outside of administrative tasks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT automation or remote software deployment.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Unknown (unclassified) binary establishes a network connection on TCP port 3389.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a custom Go backdoor establishes a network connection on RDP port 3389, enabling remote access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unknown binaries opening RDP ports are highly suspicious, as this is a common method for attackers to maintain access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only trusted, known binaries should open RDP connections.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rare for legitimate software; usually only RDP clients/servers.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses net.exe to create or manipulate user accounts, enabling persistence or privilege escalation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Frequent or scripted use of net user to add or modify accounts is a common persistence technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Account management should be infrequent and performed by administrators.
key_indicators: Multiple net user executions in short time

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Unknown binary launches PowerShell for further execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, a custom Go backdoor launches PowerShell, enabling execution of arbitrary commands or scripts.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unknown binaries launching PowerShell is a common method for executing malicious payloads or scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: PowerShell should be launched by trusted processes, not unknown binaries.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code modifies the safeboot registry keys to enable network access for a remote access tool during safeboot.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Modifying safeboot keys to enable malware persistence in safe mode is a known defense evasion technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Safe mode should only load essential drivers/services.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely used by legitimate recovery tools.

attack_chain.action: Initial access via exploitation of ProxyShell or SonicWall VPN vulnerabilities.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of backdoor and lateral movement tools

attack_chain.action: Deploy custom Go backdoor masquerading as svchost.exe, launched by a non-standard parent process.
Open RDP port 3389 via netsh to enable remote access.
Perform network reconnaissance using single pings.
attack_chain.leads_to: Identify additional targets for lateral movement

attack_chain.action: Drop additional payloads or tools via WinRM/PowerShell (wsmprovhost.exe).
Establish RDP connections from unknown binaries.
Manipulate user accounts via net.exe for persistence or privilege escalation.
Unknown binary launches PowerShell for further exploitation.
Modify safeboot registry keys to ensure malware persistence in safe mode.
Encrypt victim data for ransom (ransomware payload).

behavioral_signatures: netsh used to open RDP port 3389
Multiple net user executions in short time
file_indicators: Custom Go binaries with SHA256 hashes (see IOCs)
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known BianLian C2 IPs (see IOCs)
Single ICMP pings to multiple internal hosts
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for svchost.exe processes not launched by services.exe or running from non-standard paths. Alert on netsh commands opening RDP ports, especially from unknown processes. Detect file writes by wsmprovhost.exe and PowerShell launched by unknown binaries. Track multiple net user executions in a short period. Watch for reg.exe modifying safeboot keys. Correlate with outbound connections to known BianLian C2 IPs and unexpected RDP activity.
